e.text: A2 hits 15.9%, four times the benchmark; asking the Critic how to spend the remaining $2,300 better.

e.note: Reading results for A2, A3

critique.summary: Both plans beat the benchmark about fourfold on reach at roughly a third of the cost per point: A2 reaches 15.9% (p10 14.3%) at $800 per point against the benchmark's 4.0% at $2587. The Stüssy drop, early host reads and targeted social carry nearly all credited adoption, while $300 partner outlets and the late street teams on days 25–26 add little.

findings.finding: It is the strongest plan, at 15.9% mean reach, a 14.3% 10th percentile and $800 per point; the Stüssy drop (11.4% of adoption for $2000) and the two host reads (10.8% and 9.8% for $3450 each) do the heavy lifting.
All three partners are in West Hollywood and are credited 0.4–1.0% each, while Culver City (fit 0.88) and Inglewood (fit 0.905) get no direct seeding.
It reaches 15.2% with a weaker 13.5% 10th percentile at $823 per point; the day 25–26 street teams in Culver City (0.6%) and Inglewood (0.4%) come too late for word of mouth to spread.
Running targeted social for 20 days from day 0 lifted its credit to 12.1% for $3600, against A2's 9.2% for $2880 over 16 days, though cost per credited point is similar.
It reaches 4.0% at $2587 per point; six of its street teams are credited 0.0–0.8% each, which confirms that blind street spend wastes money.

changes.change: Start from A2 and drop partner Little Bean Cafe (CDF2E1EA, 0.4%). Move that $300 plus the unspent $2320 to street teams in zone 2 (Culver City) and zone 4 (Inglewood) on days 1–3.
changes.why: These are the highest-fit unseeded zones, and seeding them early lets word of mouth, already about 50% of adoption, compound.

changes.change: Do not run A3's late street days (street:0, street:2 and street:4 on days 25–26).
changes.why: They are credited only 0.4–1.0% each for $450, the worst cost per point in the plan.

changes.change: Extend social:city in A2 to start on day 0 and run 20 days.
changes.why: A3's longer run earned 12.1% credit against 9.2%, at a similar cost per credited point.

changes.change: Move the Brilliant Idiots read in A2 from day 10 to about day 5.
changes.why: Earlier reads give word of mouth more time to spread, which should help lift the 10th-percentile outcome.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Early podcasts, Stüssy drop and social reach ~18% of LA's natural audience
plan.summary: The bet is media plus early ground: two host reads, a Stüssy co-branded drop and city-wide social start nearly four weeks out, with street teams in Culver City and Inglewood, so word of mouth has time to build before the Wiltern show. Qloo taste data supports it: Bodega Boys (0.98), The Brilliant Idiots (0.96) and Stüssy (0.96) over-index heavily with Kendrick, SZA and ScHoolboy Q fans, and the street zones fit at 0.88 and 0.91. Our simulation built on Qloo taste data projects about 18.3% reach of the natural audience (range 16.1%–20.2%), roughly 4.6x the 4.0% benchmark at $808 versus $2,587 per point of reach, with word of mouth driving about half of adoption; this is a projection, not a guarantee.

media.why: Qloo affinity 0.96 in LA; 9.7% of adoption at the lowest media cost.

risks: Projections come from a simulation on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee; real reach could fall outside 16.1%–20.2%.
Street teams and Harun Coffee earned little simulated credit (0.5%–0.7%); watch whether they pull their weight.
Half of adoption relies on word of mouth; drop-curious people like Culver City's Devin may not convert without hearing a strong single.
Podcast and rerun-heavy districts reach only 11.6%; social ads may be scrolled past there.
measure: Ticket sales by promo code or link per channel (each podcast, Stüssy, social, partners) as share of the week's sales.
Social ad click-through and cost per click, weighted toward high-fit districts.
Partner card pickups and code redemptions at Catch One, Alibi and Harun.
Organic mentions and shares, as a proxy for word of mouth building after the podcast weeks.
